subject: Social Media
title: The Quantified Self
description: Learn The Quantified Self in one minute.

hook.text: 73 likes. Yesterday you got 120. What changed? Was the photo worse? Your brain runs the numbers.

buildup.text: Social media quantifies popularity. Before likes, you never had a number measuring your social worth.

discovery.text: Psychologists call this 'contingent self-worth'—tying your value to external metrics you can't control.

twist.text: Low likes trigger cortisol, the stress hormone. High likes trigger dopamine. Your mood becomes metric-driven.

climax.text: Some people delete low-performing posts to maintain an artificial average. The curation of self intensifies.

punchline.text: Your worth isn't a number. But it feels like one.

quiz.question: What is 'contingent self-worth'?
options: Tying personal value to external metrics
